selected_evidence.requirement: Record sudo commands with user and timestamp in a dedicated log, excluded from the general system log
selected_evidence.summary: The policy parses successfully. Test entries show full timestamps, invoking user `root`, target user, and command. Unique pre- and post-restart events produced zero matches and no line increase in `/var/log/messages`.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
selected_evidence.summary: Both pre- and post-restart checks report Alpine Linux v3.23 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts.

Healthy baseline boot ID `0687b392-1a6b-43bc-aaa3-46f67448c266` was captured, the native reboot was acknowledged, and node1 returned with boot ID `7ea4a020-e29c-456b-a672-ca3134a00a4c`. Syslog was started, sudoers validated, prior audit data persisted, and a new sudo event was recorded only in the dedicated log.

commands.command:
set -eu
umask 077
cat > /tmp/sudo-command-logging.conf <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
# Log sudo command events to a dedicated file, not the general syslog.
Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"
Defaults !syslog
Defaults log_year
ANTRIEB_EOF
visudo -cf /tmp/sudo-command-logging.conf
install -o root -g root -m 0440 /tmp/sudo-command-logging.conf /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging
rm -f /tmp/sudo-command-logging.conf
install -o root -g root -m 0600 /dev/null /var/log/sudo-commands.log
visudo -c
printf '%s\n' '--- INSTALLED CONFIG ---'
ls -l /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging /var/log/sudo-commands.log
sed -n '1,20p' /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging
